reshared_post.reshared_text:
Another short interview from my #PyTorch Conference week in Paris this time with my colleague Daniel, discussing his session:
“From Pretrained to Personal: Privacy-First Fine-Tuning on AI PCs.”

One of the key messages from his talk is simple but powerful:
The data you most want to fine-tune on is often the data you cannot upload.
Whether in healthcare, finance, government, or enterprise environments, privacy and data control are non-negotiable.

What is changing now is not incremental it’s a capability shift.
Thanks to more efficient fine-tuning methods like LoRA and QLoRA, increasingly capable AI PCs, and mature frameworks built around PyTorch, it is now possible to perform meaningful model fine-tuning fully locally keeping sensitive data inside your organization.

In this 2-minute demo interview, Daniel shows how this works in practice on the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, demonstrating that local, privacy-first AI workflows are becoming realistic for developers, researchers, and enterprises.

We also shared a preview of something we are very excited about:
the upcoming AMD AI Playbooks, a collection of guided, hands-on developer experiences designed to help people get started with local AI, fine-tuning, and other advanced workflows on modern AI hardware.

This is exactly the kind of shift we are seeing across the ecosystem:
from generic pretrained models to personalized, domain-specific models trained where the data lives.

🎥 Watch the short demo interview below — and stay tuned for the launch of the AMD AI Playbooks later this month.
